note: PRECONDITION: this predicate is only meaningful on an input that declares a global resource named bound* which the atomic or the buffer load is required to reach. repro.hlsl, control-bound-only.hlsl, control-separate-vars.hlsl, defect2.hlsl, defect3.hlsl and defect4.hlsl all satisfy that; defect5.hlsl deliberately does NOT (it has no bound resource at all) and is therefore scored by match-invalid-spirv.json instead. That is not hypothetical: defect5 was first captured under this predicate and scored `repro` purely because clause 3 is vacuous when nothing is named bound*. The control caught it -- exactly the #3009 hazard of a predicate that matches things it should not. WHAT IT ENCODES: the reported symptom is a SILENT miscompile, so there is no exit code to key on and the predicate has to read the emitted SPIR-V. Per the issue, the VarDecl alias makes every use of `mixed` re-lower as a fresh OpUntypedAccessChainKHR over the recorded heap index, the variable's own storage becomes dead, and 'the bound resource is dropped from the module entirely'. So: (1) a module was emitted and the atomic (image case) or the buffer load (defect 4 case) survived, (2) a heap access chain is present, (3) the bound resource the source assigns is not in the module at all. Clause 3 is an absence clause, which triage.py's _is_absence_predicate detects, so a probe that 'matches' while also failing to compile is reclassified invalid-probe -- the #1877 trap. CONTROLS, both captured with --expect no-match. variant-bound-only-main-debug.txt is repro.hlsl with the heap assignment deleted; it is the one that actually runs on the ground-truth build (exit 0), so it exercises the predicate against real known-good SPIR-V -- it emits '%boundTex = OpVariable' and 'OpImageTexelPointer %_ptr_Image_uint %boundTex' and does not fire. variant-separate-vars-main-debug.txt is the reporter's own documented workaround (heap and bound in separate variables): on a build where the heap path works it carries BOTH positive markers and is separated from the symptom only by %boundTex still being present, which is what would prove clauses 1+2 alone do not discriminate -- but on main-debug it fails validation before emitting anything, so today it is a weak control and the load-bearing one is bound-only. variant-vd-repro-main-debug.txt and variant-vd-defect2-main-debug.txt add -Vd so the module main-debug really generates becomes visible; both keep %boundTex and both score no-match, which is far stronger evidence than a failed compile that main-debug is not silently miscompiling. ASSUMES OpName debug info is present (it is, by default; do not add -Qstrip_debug or -fspv-debug=none to cmd.txt without revisiting clause 3).
